answer:
Edgar Allan Poe, the author of the poem "Annabel Lee," enlisted in the U.S. Army on **May 26, 1827**. 

At the time of enlistment, though only 18 years old, he falsified his age as 22 and used the alias "Edgar Perry." He served for approximately one year and eight months until his discharge in April 1829, which occurred in exchange for an opportunity to attend the United States Military Academy at West Point.
